refuted_claims.claim: The task's default stance — "something here breaks a plugin at runtime"; specifically that one of the 14 required MU/TH/UR commands would fail to parse against the delivered muthur-cn.json.
refuted_claims.why_wrong: No required command breaks — not even before my fix. The lang file cannot reach any of the dispatch regexes: all 12 anchored command regexes (main.js:1257, 1275, 1288, 1302, 1313, 1329, 1345, 1353, 1364) and the 12 prefix-strip regexes in handleSpecialOrder (main.js:4567-4579) are hardcoded ASCII/French literals in JS. The only localization-reachable parse surface is MOTHER.Keywords.*, and the translator had left MOTHER.Keywords.Special as the byte 'SPECIAL', which is exactly the token that carries the 3-word form. So `SPECIAL ORDER 937` resolved via specialWords.includes('SPECIAL') && orderWords.includes('ORDER'), and orderWords/protocolWords each carry a hardcoded English fallback ('ORDER' at main.js:1150, 'PROTOCOL' at :1158) that no lang file can remove.

verdict:
Phase 3 is sound. It does NOT break a plugin at runtime — I found one real functional defect (not a blocking one), two structural gaps, and one stale doc; all four are now fixed and negative-tested. Item by item: 1. MU/TH/UR PARSER — PASS, but with one genuine defect found and fixed. I extracted the full token surface myself: 12 anchored dispatch regexes plus 12 prefix-strip regexes, ALL hardcoded ASCII/French literals in main.js, therefore untouchable by any lang file. The single localization-reachable parse surface is MOTHER.Keywords.* (4 read points, main.js:1148/1152/1153/1156). Simulating the real dispatch chain: all 14 required commands routed correctly AND resolved (SPECIAL ORDER 937 and bare 937 both yield orderKey '937'; CERBERUS yields 'CERBERUS'), and /M round-trips CJK intact. That held even before my fix, because the translator happened to leave Special='SPECIAL' and because orderWords/protocolWords carry hardcoded English fallbacks. But three tokens WERE translated, which widened the acceptance gate without widening the resolver — admitting 4 Chinese forms that dead-end, and for un-hacked players firing a spurious MUTHUR.SpecialOrderAttempt intrusion alert at the GM. Reverted to upstream bytes. 2. KEY COVERAGE AND NAMESPACE — PASS, all four. muthur 276/275 upstream keys covered, motiontracker 69/69, babele 102/102; placeholders 1:1 across all three; zero ALIENRPG.* leakage; zero namespace escapes; zero dead keys. tah-alien-cn.json is still exactly '{}' and correctly so — upstream's own languages/en.json is `{"tokenActionHud":{}}` with 0 keys, its source reads only 5 ALIENRPG.* keys, and I verified all 5 are already translated in lang/cn.json. One apparent anomaly (MotionTracker.motionless sitting outside the MOTIONTRACKER namespace) is a false positive: upstream genuinely ships two casings of that namespace. 3. MODULE GATE — PASS. Re-read #filterLanguagePaths (localization.mjs:331-339): the test is `game.modules.get(l.module)?.active`, an exact id match. Byte-compared all four declared gates against the installed module.json ids: alien-mu-th-ur (14/14), motion_tracker (14/14), token-action-hud-alien (22/22), babele (6/6) — all equal. I also traced two mechanisms the audit doc did not: files are merged with mergeObject after expandObject (so flat-dotted and nested files are equivalent — motiontracker/babele are fully flat, muthur/cn.json fully nested, none mixed, no leaf-that-is-also-branch), and setLanguage:233-236 loads a separate English fallback, so a missing key degrades to English rather than to a raw key. 4. BLAST RADIUS — PASS. The existing suite is green (adversarial 397/0, positive 115/0), but I did not take its word for it: I re-measured independently over the real corpus of 5568 files across 296 installed packages. All 13 channel-A literal keys resolve to exactly one owner matching their declared `requires`; all 4 channel-D button classes and their English strings are owned only by modules:terminal; all 9 channel-E `>text` needles likewise; and the 4 channel-C notification regexes matched literals from at most one package. Zero patterns with more than one owner. 5. CJK TERMINAL WIDTH — VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, decision correct. First the empirical fact: there is no pipe-bordered table in ANY delivered file (0 pipe/box-drawing strings across all three, and 0 pipes in upstream en.json), and no padEnd/column code anywhere in MU/TH/UR. The real question is terminal.js:1147 generateTable, and I checked all three of its claims rather than accepting them. (a) It IS broken by CJK — computing UAX#11 East-Asian widths on its actual output, a row with a Chinese cell renders 41 columns against 36 for every other row; pure-ASCII rows render a uniform 47. (b) It IS unreachable — 1 declaration inside initCLI's body and 6 call sites, no assignment to any object, so the only patch route would be wrapping String.prototype.padEnd globally. (c) None of the 13 translated strings reach it — I read all 6 call sites: they consume el.dataset.targetTile, el.dataset.wallName, and .terminal-journal-page textContent, and none of the 4 relabeled button classes is queried by any of them. The strings we do ship are all 2-column-per-char CJK, but they render as

text and button textContent, never as padEnd-aligned cells. The documented decision to leave generateTable alone, and the honest note that translating journal page names will later skew `ls`, are both correct. 6. OVERCLAIM — one found and fixed, plus confirmation the earlier one was already closed. The CI hole that let v0.1.0 ship four {} shells was genuinely fixed this phase (release.yml now checks lang/plugins/*.json with a documented ALLOW_EMPTY for tah-alien) — I replicated the gate locally and it behaves correctly. The remaining mismatch is the inverse of last phase's: README:20-21 still declared the three files empty shells when they are populated. Its numeric claims elsewhere hold exactly (600 cn keys / 590 en keys / 584 covered, all MATCH). ONE THING FOR YOU TO DECIDE, NOT A DEFECT: module.json is still version 0.1.0 while the working tree now differs materially from the published v0.1.0 (three populated lang files, a hardened CI gate, and today's fixes). I deliberately did not bump it — that is a release call. The README now states plainly that the filled files ship with the next release and that published v0.1.0 contains the shells, so the tree is honest either way; but the next release must carry a version bump or the download URL / changelog assertions in the workflow will fail against the tag.
